title: Bacterial 16S rRNA Tree
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Bacterial 16S rRNA Tree scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: A rooted branching tree visibly shows the stated sister taxa and their clade relationships.
Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary to encode the supplied evolutionary distances.
The named taxa are legible at the tree tips.
The named clade is visibly highlighted distinctly from the rest of the tree.
A visible scale or distance label identifies the evolutionary-distance interpretation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/rectangular exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents a rooted rectangular phylogram with the required topology, proportional horizontal branch lengths, five legible taxa, distinct Proteobacteria highlighting, and an explicit substitutions/site scale.

items.evidence: Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa form one sister pair; Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus form another; Mycobacterium tuberculosis branches separately from the same rooted backbone.
Solid horizontal branches visibly vary in length consistently with the supplied distances; dashed label-alignment extensions are explicitly identified as adding no branch length.
All five named taxa are large, legible, and aligned with their corresponding tree tips.
The Escherichia coli–Pseudomonas aeruginosa clade is distinctly shown in blue and labeled Proteobacteria with a blue bracket.
A visible scale bar is labeled “0.05 substitutions/site,” and the diagram also states that horizontal distance represents substitutions/site.
